meta.title: Master · Part 2 · Open cloze
meta.provenance: From the pantry drafts cloze.js–cloze4.js (original sentences). Reviewed item by item in October 2026: every gap checked for other words that also fit, and nine items given the extra answers a correct student could write. Frequencies are counted from the 713 gaps of the 59 open-cloze passages in data/use-of-english/gapfill.

items.s: She is very good ___ solving puzzles.
items.why: Good at + -ing.

items.s: I am looking forward ___ seeing you next week.
items.why: Look forward to + -ing.

items.s: He apologised ___ being late.
items.why: Apologise for.

items.s: Many students depend ___ their parents for money.
items.why: Depend on.

items.s: The teacher was proud ___ her class.
items.why: Proud of.

items.s: We were surprised ___ the news.
items.why: Surprised at or by.

items.s: There is no point ___ arguing about it.
items.why: No point in + -ing.

items.s: She is interested ___ learning Japanese.
items.why: Interested in.

items.s: What is the reason ___ this delay?
items.why: Reason for.

items.s: ___ it was raining, we went for a walk.
items.why: Although + a full clause.

items.s: We went out ___ the bad weather.
items.why: Despite + a noun phrase. Although needs a clause.

items.s: I will call you as soon ___ I arrive.
items.why: As soon as.

items.s: He studied hard in ___ to pass.
items.why: In order to.

items.s: She did not go out ___ she had finished her homework.
items.why: Until gives the time when something changes.

items.s: He is rich; ___, he is not happy.
items.why: However links two ideas and takes a comma.

items.s: We will be late ___ we leave now.
items.why: Unless means if not.

items.s: I wish I ___ more time to study.
items.why: Wish + past tense for a present regret.

items.s: He was made ___ stay after school.
items.why: Passive of make takes a to-infinitive.

items.s: You ___ better see a doctor about that cough.
items.why: Had better + bare infinitive.

items.s: Not only ___ she win the race, but she also broke the record.
items.why: Inversion after not only needs an auxiliary.

items.s: The window ___ broken last night.
items.why: Passive, past simple.

items.s: He asked me ___ I could help him.
items.why: Reported yes/no question.

items.s: The girl ___ sits next to me is my cousin.
items.why: Who for people as the subject.

items.s: That is the man ___ car was stolen.
items.why: Whose shows possession.

items.s: This is the house ___ I grew up.
items.why: Where for places.

items.s: She told me about her trip, ___ sounded amazing.
items.why: Which refers back to the whole idea.

items.s: I will never forget the day ___ we met.
items.why: When for times.

items.s: There is not ___ milk left in the fridge.
items.why: Any in negatives. Milk is uncountable.

items.s: I have ___ friends in this city, so I feel lonely.
items.why: Few + countable nouns, with a negative feeling.

items.s: How ___ time do we have left?
items.why: Much with uncountable nouns.

items.s: I tried both options, but ___ of them worked.
items.why: Neither is for two things. Watch the spelling: neither.

items.s: ___ of my friends lives near me; they all live far away.
items.why: None is for more than two.

items.s: She is old ___ to drive.
items.why: Enough comes after the adjective. Watch the spelling: enough.

items.s: At first I did not like him, but I got used ___ his jokes.
items.why: Get used to + noun or -ing.

items.s: I would rather stay home ___ go out tonight.
items.why: Would rather ... than. Not then.

items.s: As far ___ I know, the shop closes at six.
items.why: As far as I know.

items.s: She has been working here ___ 2019.
items.why: Since + a point in time.

items.s: He did it on ___ because he wanted to annoy me.
items.why: On purpose.

items.s: I cannot find my keys. Can you help me look ___ them?
items.why: Look for means search.

items.s: The meeting was called ___ because the manager was ill.
items.why: Call off means cancel.

items.s: She grew ___ in a small village.
items.why: Grow up.

items.s: We ran ___ of milk, so I went to the shop.
items.why: Run out of.

items.s: By the time we arrived, the film ___ already started.
items.why: Past perfect: an action finished before another past action.

items.s: The new bridge has ___ built to reduce traffic in the town centre.
items.why: Present perfect passive: has been + past participle.

items.s: The results will ___ announced on Friday.
items.why: Future passive: will be + past participle.

items.s: She hates ___ laughed at.
items.why: Passive gerund: being + past participle, after verbs like hate, like and avoid.

items.s: I ___ not realise how late it was until I looked at the clock.
items.why: Past simple negative: did + not + base verb.

items.s: She enjoys swimming, and so ___ her brother.
items.why: So + auxiliary + subject. The auxiliary matches the first verb: enjoys, so does.

items.s: Our teacher ___ to be a professional dancer before she started teaching.
items.why: Used to describes past states. Would cannot be used for states like be.

items.s: It ___ have been Tom who phoned; he is abroad this week.
items.why: Cannot have + past participle: you are sure it was impossible.

items.s: I should ___ listened to your advice.
items.why: Should have + past participle: a past regret or mistake.

items.s: Yesterday we ___ to wait an hour for a table.
items.why: The past of have to is had to. Must has no past form.

items.s: All the players ___ been asked to bring a passport, so please check yours.
items.why: Present perfect passive with a plural subject: have been asked.

items.s: By this time next year, I ___ have lived here for ten years.
items.why: Future perfect: will have + past participle.

items.s: Little ___ she know that the exam had been cancelled.
items.why: Negative adverbials such as little, never and hardly are followed by inversion with an auxiliary.

items.s: Nobody showed Tom how to play the guitar, so he taught ___.
items.why: Reflexive pronoun: the subject and the object are the same person.

items.s: We really enjoyed ___ at the party.
items.why: Enjoy + reflexive pronoun. Watch the plural: ourselves.

items.s: The two friends have known each ___ for years.
items.why: Each other: a reciprocal pronoun.

items.s: ___ was raining so heavily that we stayed indoors.
items.why: It is the subject for weather, time and distance.

items.s: ___ used to be a cinema on this street.
items.why: There + be introduces something that exists or existed.

items.s: My phone fell in the sea, so I had to buy a new ___.
items.why: One replaces a countable noun when it is a different thing. It would mean the same phone.

items.s: The museum, ___ opened in 1998, attracts thousands of visitors every year.
items.why: After a comma (non-defining clause) use which, not that.

items.s: The woman to ___ I spoke was very helpful.
items.why: Preposition + whom for people.

items.s: I could not understand ___ he was saying.
items.why: What means the thing that.

items.s: I felt so ill that I did not eat ___ all day.
items.why: Anything in negative sentences. Nothing would make a double negative.

items.s: Many students prefer working in groups because it helps ___ to learn from each other.
items.why: Object pronoun after helps.

items.s: The city is famous for ___ ancient walls.
items.why: Its, with no apostrophe, is the possessive of it.

items.s: We visited four countries in two weeks, and ___ one was very different.
items.why: Each or every + one, for the items in a group taken separately.

items.s: We have not finished yet, so we need ___ ten minutes.
items.why: Another + number + plural noun means that many more.

items.s: Some people prefer cities, while ___ prefer the countryside.
items.why: Others means other people. No noun follows.

items.s: I have two brothers, and ___ of them are doctors, like me.
items.why: Both of + plural pronoun, for two people.

items.s: I spent the ___ weekend revising for the exam.
items.why: The whole + singular noun. All would not follow the.

items.s: It rained ___ day yesterday, so we stayed in.
items.why: All day means from morning to night.

items.s: Who is ___ best player in your team?
items.why: The before a superlative.

items.s: Hardly ___ people came to the concert, so it was cancelled.
items.why: Hardly any means almost none.

items.s: There is not ___ point in complaining about it now.
items.why: Not much or not any with uncountable nouns.

items.s: I have ___ few friends who live nearby, so I see them quite often.
items.why: A few is positive (some). Few alone is negative (hardly any).

items.s: ___ four years, the Olympic Games take place in a different country.
items.why: Every + number + plural noun for regular intervals.

items.s: I have ___ idea what he is talking about.
items.why: No idea. Not and none cannot go directly before a noun.

items.s: I wonder ___ the shop is open on Sundays.
items.why: If or whether introduces an indirect yes/no question.

items.s: She looked at me as ___ nothing had happened.
items.why: As though or as if + past perfect for an unreal comparison.

items.s: She speaks French and German, as ___ as English.
items.why: As well as means and also.

items.s: Some people love big cities, ___ others prefer village life.
items.why: While or whereas shows a contrast between two groups.

items.s: She spoke slowly ___ that everyone could understand.
items.why: So that + clause shows purpose.

items.s: Take an umbrella in ___ it rains.
items.why: In case + clause: as a precaution.

items.s: You can borrow my car as ___ as you drive carefully.
items.why: As long as means on condition that.

items.s: Hurry up, ___ you will miss the bus.
items.why: Otherwise means if you do not.

items.s: I did not go to the party. ___, I stayed at home and read a book.
items.why: Instead means in place of the thing just mentioned.

items.s: I will not change my mind, even ___ you ask me again.
items.why: Even if + a possible future situation.

items.s: I cannot decide ___ to accept the job or not.
items.why: Whether + to-infinitive. If cannot be used here.

items.s: ___ hard I try, I cannot open this jar.
items.why: However + adjective or adverb means no matter how.

items.s: It was not ___ I got home that I realised I had lost my wallet.
items.why: Not until marks the point when something first happened.

items.s: He was ___ tired that he fell asleep at his desk.
items.why: So + adjective + that + result.

items.s: It was ___ a beautiful day that we decided to have a picnic.
items.why: Such + a + adjective + noun + that + result.

items.s: I was ___ surprised to say anything.
items.why: Too + adjective + to-infinitive means more than is needed to do it.

items.s: The film was far better ___ I expected.
items.why: Comparative + than. Watch the spelling: than, not then.

items.s: She is not as tall ___ her sister.
items.why: Not as + adjective + as.

items.s: The harder you work, ___ better your results will be.
items.why: The + comparative, the + comparative.

items.s: The longer the journey, the ___ tired we became.
items.why: The + comparative, the + comparative. Tired takes more.

items.s: This is by far the ___ difficult exam I have ever taken.
items.why: Superlative of a long adjective: the most + adjective.

items.s: The new model is ___ more expensive than the old one.
items.why: Much, far, even or still can strengthen a comparative. Very cannot.

items.s: No sooner had we sat down ___ the waiter brought the menu.
items.why: No sooner ... than. Hardly ... when is the matching pair.

items.s: I try to eat ___ sugar than I used to.
items.why: Less with uncountable nouns. Fewer is for countable nouns.

items.s: There were so ___ people at the concert that we could not move.
items.why: So many + countable noun + that + result.

items.s: Many people are afraid ___ flying.
items.why: Afraid of.

items.s: We enjoyed the trip in spite ___ the rain.
items.why: In spite of + noun phrase.

items.s: The match was cancelled because ___ the weather.
items.why: Because of + noun phrase. Because alone needs a clause.

items.s: Why not walk instead ___ taking the bus?
items.why: Instead of + noun or -ing.

items.s: She has been famous ___ her cooking since she won a TV competition.
items.why: Famous for.

items.s: I have not seen her ___ three weeks.
items.why: For + a length of time.

items.s: This design is similar ___ the one we used last year.
items.why: Similar to.

items.s: In addition ___ English, she speaks Italian and Greek.
items.why: In addition to + noun or -ing.

items.s: We were introduced ___ each other at the party.
items.why: Introduce someone to someone.

items.s: I am not familiar ___ this software.
items.why: Familiar with.

items.s: The book was written ___ a famous Spanish author.
items.why: By + the agent in a passive sentence.

items.s: Heavy rain prevented us ___ leaving the house.
items.why: Prevent someone from + -ing.

items.s: ___ to the forecast, it will snow tomorrow.
items.why: According to + a source of information.

items.s: ___ from Maria, everybody passed the test.
items.why: Apart from means except for.

items.s: I am worried ___ my exam results.
items.why: Worried about.

items.s: She specialises ___ marine biology.
items.why: Specialise in.

items.s: Over two hundred runners took ___ in the charity race.
items.why: Take part in means participate.

items.s: We set ___ at dawn to avoid the traffic.
items.why: Set off or set out means begin a journey.

items.s: Scientists carried ___ a series of experiments on the new drug.
items.why: Carry out means do and complete a task.

items.s: The weather turned ___ to be much better than the forecast.
items.why: Turn out to be describes a surprising result.

items.s: She decided to give ___ smoking last year.
items.why: Give up means stop doing something.

items.s: I came ___ my old diary while I was tidying the attic.
items.why: Come across means find by chance.

items.s: Can you find ___ what time the train leaves?
items.why: Find out means discover information.

items.s: If you keep spending money like that, you will end ___ broke.
items.why: End up + adjective means finally be in a situation.

items.s: The manager promised to deal ___ the complaint immediately.
items.why: Deal with means take action about.

items.s: I get ___ very well with my new colleagues.
items.why: Get on or get along means have a good relationship.

items.s: Nothing can make ___ for the time we have lost.
items.why: Make up for means compensate for.

items.s: I cannot put up ___ this noise any longer.
items.why: Put up with means tolerate.

items.s: On the other ___, the journey was cheaper than expected.
items.why: On the one hand ... on the other hand.

items.s: In the ___, we decided to stay at home.
items.why: In the end means finally.

items.s: At ___, we did not understand the rules, but later it became clear.
items.why: At first contrasts with later.

items.s: As a ___, many shops had to close.
items.why: As a result introduces a consequence.

items.s: It was a difficult choice, but ___ the whole I think we chose well.
items.why: On the whole means in general.

items.s: By the ___, did you remember to buy the tickets?
items.why: By the way adds a new or less important topic.

items.s: I cannot come. I have too much work and, ___ any case, I do not feel well.
items.why: In any case means whatever happens.

items.s: You can stay with us for the time ___.
items.why: For the time being means for now, but not permanently.

items.s: The doctor will see you soon. In the ___, please take a seat.
items.why: In the meantime means while waiting.

items.s: Some animals, for ___, sleep standing up.
items.why: For example or for instance introduces an illustration.

items.s: I broke the vase by ___; I did not mean to.
items.why: By accident is the opposite of on purpose.

items.s: The wedding will take ___ in a small church.
items.why: Events take place. People take part.

items.s: Please make ___ that you lock the door when you leave.
items.why: Make sure or make certain.

items.s: Students must pay ___ to the teacher during lessons.
items.why: Pay attention to.

items.s: It was lovely to meet you. Let us keep in ___.
items.why: Keep in touch means stay in contact.

items.s: You should take ___ of the good weather and go for a walk.
items.why: Take advantage of.

items.s: She has made great ___ in her English this year.
items.why: Make progress. Watch the spelling: progress.

items.s: Social media plays a major ___ in how young people communicate.
items.why: Play a part or play a role.

items.s: He caught ___ of a rare bird as he walked through the forest.
items.why: Catch sight of means see suddenly.

items.s: It is important to do your ___ to protect the environment.
items.why: Do your best, or do your bit.

items.s: The company went out of ___ after thirty years.
items.why: Go out of business means stop trading.

items.s: He suggested ___ to the beach for the day.
items.why: Suggest + -ing.

items.s: She admitted ___ the window.
items.why: Admit + -ing.

items.s: She is said ___ be the richest woman in Europe.
items.why: Passive reporting: is said to + infinitive.

items.s: My parents want me ___ become a doctor.
items.why: Want someone to + infinitive.

items.s: He told me ___ he would call me the next day.
items.why: Reported statement: told someone that + clause.

items.s: She ___ me that she was moving to Canada.
items.why: Tell is followed by a person. Say is not.

items.s: He spoke quietly so ___ not to wake the baby.
items.why: So as (not) to + infinitive shows purpose.

items.s: I look forward to ___ from you soon.
items.why: Look forward to + -ing, because to is a preposition here.

items.s: I prefer tea ___ coffee.
items.why: Prefer one thing to another.

items.s: He insisted ___ paying for the meal.
items.why: Insist on + -ing.
